description: Use this skill when designing the UX and content strategy for a Salesforce-powered self-service portal or help center — pre-deflection article surfacing, Help Center search UX, friction-calibrated case submission forms, community peer support layers, and deflection measurement. Trigger keywords: design self-service portal, case deflection strategy, help center UX design, reduce support volume with self-service, knowledge base search experience. NOT for picking which contact reasons to deflect and through which channel — use architect/case-deflection-strategy. NOT for building the Experience Cloud site itself — use admin/experience-cloud-site-setup. More trigger keywords: article visibility matrix IsVisibleInCsp IsVisibleInPkb, which articles show in the customer portal, case visibility for portal users, CaseComment IsPublished customer visible comment, self-registration profile and account for a portal, Help Center template does not support login, deflection metrics SOQL KnowledgeArticleViewStat, self-service journey map, moderation policy for a support community.
inputs: Current inbound case volume by contact reason (from Case reports or Einstein Conversation Mining)
Existing knowledge article inventory: count, category coverage, average age
Portal audience: authenticated customers vs. unauthenticated public visitors
Deflection goal: target reduction percentage or absolute case volume target
Available channels: Help Center, Community (peer support), Einstein Bot, email-to-case
name: self-service-design
official_sources: **Metadata API Developer Guide**, `Network` (<https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/262/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/api_meta.pdf>) — the `selfRegistration` / `selfRegProfile` pair, `networkMemberGroups`, `caseCommentEmailTemplate`, `enableTopicAssignmentRules`, `allowMembersToFlag` and the `status` enum behind the self-registration, moderation and release decisions (Gotchas 9 and 10; worked-examples.md §6)

**Metadata API Developer Guide**, `ExperienceBundle` and `NavigationMenu` — `loginAppPageId` / `forgotPasswordRouteId` / `selfRegistrationRouteId` "Unsupported if the active Experience Builder template for the site doesn't support login (such as Help Center)", the `templateName` and theme lists, and "The Help Center and LWR templates … don't include generic record pages" (Gotcha 6; the template row in Decision Guidance)

**Metadata API Developer Guide**, `KnowledgeSettings`, `ModerationRule`, `KeywordList`, `ManagedTopics`, `CommunitiesSettings`, `SharingSet` and `SharingRules` — `useSuggestedArticlesForCase` and its `caseFields`, the `showArticleSummaries*` switches, the 30-per-org moderation and keyword ceilings, the 25-topic browse cap, `enablePowerCustomerCaseStatus`, the sharing-set licence list, and `SharingGuestRule.accessLevel` "can be set only to `Read`" (Gotchas 10 and 11; the article-quality-versus-UX tradeoff; worked-examples.md §3, §4, §7)

**Object Reference**, `Knowledge__kav`, `KnowledgeArticleViewStat` and `KnowledgeArticleVoteStat` (<https://resources.docs.salesforce.com/262/latest/en-us/sfdc/pdf/object_reference.pdf>) — the four Required visibility booleans and their Create/Update properties, and the `Channel` picklist (`AllChannels`, `App`, `Pkb`, `Csp`, `Prm`), `ViewCount` as unique views, and `NormalizedScore` as relative and time-weighted (Gotcha 4; the Adaptable measurement loop; worked-examples.md §3, §5)

**Object Reference**, `Case`, `CaseComment`, `CaseArticle` and `NetworkSelfRegistration` — `Case.IsVisibleInSelfService` "does not alter sharing"; `CaseComment.IsPublished` as "the only CaseComment field that can be updated via the API"; `CaseArticle` inaccessible to Customer Portal users; self-registering users "required to be associated with an account … only one account per Experience Cloud site" (Gotchas 7, 8 and 9; the Trusted pillar's exposure argument)

**Salesforce App Limits Cheat Sheet**, "Total API Request Allocations" — the per-licence API rows (`Customer Community: 0`, `Customer Community Login: 0`, `Customer Community Plus: 200`, `Partner Community: 200`) that make the licence a design input, and the absence of any Experience Cloud sizing rows, which the guide defers with "For Experience Cloud limits, see Experience Cloud User Licenses" (worked-examples.md §1)

**`standards/decision-trees/sharing-selection.md`** (repo) — routes the Mechanism column of the exposed-object table between OWD, role hierarchy, sharing rules, sharing sets and Apex managed sharing rather than this skill re-deriving it (Recommended Workflow step 3; worked-examples.md §4)

**`skills/admin/case-management-setup/references/worked-example-case-intake.md`** (repo) — the Acme intake this design sits in front of: the queues, escalation rule, entitlement process and org-wide address that the self-service journeys feed
**Salesforce Well-Architected Overview** — <https://architect.salesforce.com/docs/architect/well-architected/guide/overview.html> — architecture quality framing (Easy, Adaptable, Trusted pillars)

**Deflect Cases with Self-Service** and **Provide a Self-Service Help Center** — help.salesforce.com — the original authority behind this skill's Case Deflection component and Help Center template claims. UNVERIFIED (2026-09-05): help.salesforce.com cannot be fetched from this environment, and neither the Metadata API Developer Guide nor the Object Reference names the Case Deflection component, so those claims carry markers where they are stated.
outputs: Self-service portal design brief covering UX structure, deflection mechanisms, and measurement plan
Pre-deflection article surfacing specification for case submission form
Friction calibration recommendation for the case submission flow
Deflection rate measurement setup using Case Deflection component
Self-service design YAML (journeys, exposed objects and their sharing mechanisms, article visibility matrix, self-registration and moderation decisions, metrics, acceptance tests)
Article visibility matrix mapping each channel to its Knowledge__kav flag
